cohort: The study participants were primiparous women who had either a full-term cesarean section or vaginal delivery.
finding: The vaginal delivery group had a higher incidence of pelvic floor dysfunction and damage to both Type I and Type II muscle fibers in the early postpartum period compared to the cesarean section group, which was primarily associated with Type I muscle fiber damage.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was associated with a higher incidence of pelvic floor dysfunction and damage to both Type I and Type II muscle fibers, whereas cesarean section was primarily associated with Type I muscle fiber damage.
